text.0_Siman: Rabbi Nechunia ben Hakana said, "One verse states, 'And now men see not the light which is bright in the skies,' (Job 37:21). Another verse states, 'He made darkness His hiding-place' (Psalms 18:12). And it says, 'Clouds and darkness surround Him' (Psalms 97:2). This is a difficulty. A third scripture reconciles them: 'Even the darkness is not too dark for You, But the night shines as the day; the darkness is as the light' (Psalms 139:12)."
text.1_Siman: Rabbi Berechiah said, "It is written, 'Now the earth was tohu and bohu' (Genesis 1:2). What does 'was' mean? That the tohu already was. What is tohu? Something that confounds [m'taha] people. And what is bohu? Tohu was, and it returned to bohu. And what is bohu? A thing that has substance in it, as is written, 'It is inside it [bo hu].'"
text.2_Siman: [Rabbi Berechiah continued,] "And why does the Torah begin with [the letter] Bet? To start with a blessing [b'racha]. From this, we learn that the Torah is called a blessing, as it is said, 'Full [with the] blessing of YHVH, possess the sea and the south' (Deuteronomy 33:23). There is no sea other than Torah, as it is said, 'And broader than the sea' (Job 11:9). And what is 'Full with the blessing of God'? It means that every place that [the letter] Bet is said is the language of blessing. As we say, 'b'reishit'. And there is no beginning [ראשית] except wisdom, as it is said, 'The beginning [ראשית] of wisdom is the fear of YHVH' (Psalms 111:10). And there is no wisdom except [as the result of a] blessing, as it is said, 'And Elohim blessed Solomon,' and it is written, 'YHVH gave wisdom to Solomon' (1 Kings 5:26). This is comparable to a king that marries his daughter to his son and says to him [the son] at the wedding, 'Do with her as you will.'"
text.3_Siman: [Rabbi Berechiah continued,] "And what is the proof that this 'b'rachah' is from the word 'blessing' [baruch]? Perhaps it is from the language of [the word] 'knee' [berech]. As it is written, 'For to Me every knee will bend' (Isaiah 45:23). [God is] the Place [towards which] all knees bend. To what parable is this similar? To people who seek to see the face of the king, but do not know where His house is. First, they ask, 'Where is the house of the king?', and afterward [they can ask], 'Where is the king?' Therefore [it is written], 'For to Me every knee will bend' — even the highest ones — 'Every tongue will swear [loyalty to God]' (Isaiah 45:23)."
text.4_Siman: Rabbi Rachumai sat and expounded, "Why is it written 'And filled with the blessing of YHVH, inherit the sea and the south' (Deuteronomy 33:23)? In every place [where there is the letter] Bet, it is blessed. 'It' is the filling, as it is said, 'And the filling is the blessing of YHVH.' From there, the needy drink, and from the filling [God] took counsel in the beginning. To what parable is this similar? To a king who wants to build his palace in strong cliffs. He cut stones and chiseled boulders, and a spring of great waters — living waters — went out from it. The king said, 'Since I have waters bursting forth, I will plant a garden and I will delight in it — I and the whole world.' This is as it is written, 'And I was with Him as a confidant, and I was a source of delight every day [יום יום], to rejoice before Him at all times' (Proverbs 8:30). The Torah said, 'For two thousand years I was in the bosom of the Blessed Holy One,' as it is said 'A day, a day [יום יום]'. A day of the Blessed Holy One is a thousand years, as it is said, 'For a thousand years in Your eyes is like a yesterday that has passed' (Psalms 90:4). From then on, it is for times — as it is said, 'At every time' — but the remainder is for the world — as it is said, 'And I will breathe my praise to you' (Isaiah 48:9). What does it mean 'my praise'? As it is written, 'A song of praise of David, I will raise You high' (Psalms 145:1) Why is it 'praise'? Because 'I will raise You high.' And what is this elevation? Because 'I will bless Your name forever' (Psalms 145:2)."
text.5_Siman: [Rabbi Rachumai continued,] "And what is a 'blessing'? To what parable is this comparable? To a king that plants trees in his garden, and even though rain always comes down and waters [them], and the land is damp and constantly waters them, still, he needs to water the trees from the spring. As it is said, 'The beginning of wisdom is the fear of YHVH, good intelligence to all who do them' (Psalms 111:10). And lest you say that it lacks something, it continues, 'His praise stands forever' (Psalms 111:10)."
text.6_Siman: Rabbi Amorai sat and expounded, "Why is it written 'And full of the blessing of YHVH, he will take possession of the west and south' (Deuteronomy 33:23)? Thus Moses said, 'If you walk in His laws, you will inherit this world and the next world.' The world to come is compared to the sea, as it is said 'And [it is] wider than the sea' (Job 11:9). And this world is compared to the south, as it is said '[Give me a blessing,] for you have placed me in the land of the Negev [the southern desert]' (Joshua 15:19), and from our targum [this is translated into Aramaic as], 'Behold, the earth is the south' (Targum Jonathan, Joshua 15:19)."
text.7_Siman: [Rabbi Amorai continued,] "And further, why did the Blessed Holy One add the [letter] hey in Abraham [when God changed Abram’s name to Abraham] rather than any other letter? In order that all the organs of man (Adam) will merit life in the world to come, which is compared to the sea [Ed.: Hebrew manuscripts often read "day," but it likely should be "sea." See above, #7]. So to speak, 'With him [Abraham] the building [i.e. - the structure of man] was completed.' As it is written, 'For in the image of Elohim, he made the Adam' (Genesis 9:6). Abraham in gematria is 248, which is the number of the organs of an adam."
text.8_Siman: [Rabbi Amorai continued,] "Why is it written 'He will inherit (ירשה)' (Deuteronomy 33:23)? It would have sufficed to say 'inherit' (רש) [in the imperative form]. Rather, even the Blessed Holy One is included, and thus, it is, 'inherit Yah [ירשה = רש יה]. To what is this comparable? To a king who had two treasuries and set aside one of them. After many days [literally, 'at the end days'], he said to his son, 'Take what there is in these two treasuries.' The son said, 'Perhaps he did not give me what he set aside.' He [the king] said, ‘Take everything.' And so it was written 'West and south, inherit Yah' (Deuteronomy 33:23) Inherit Yah and He will give you everything — if only you would guard My way."
text.9_Siman: Rabbi Bun said, "Why is it written 'I was set up from eternity [מעולם], from the beginning [מראש], before the earth' (Proverbs 8:23)? What is 'from eternity [מעולם]'? That it must be concealed [להעלימו] from the whole world. As it is written, '[God] also puts eternity [העולם] in their hearts [i.e. - minds]' (Ecclesiastes 3:11) — Don’t read 'eternity [העולם], rather 'hidden [העלם]. The Torah said, 'I was first, [in order] to be head [ראש] of the world,' as it is said 'I was set up from eternity, from a head [מראש].' And if you would say, 'Perhaps the earth preceded her,' the Torah says 'From before the earth' (Proverbs 8:23), as it is said, 'In the beginning [בראשית], Elohim created the Heaven and the Earth' (Genesis 1:1). And why does it say 'created'? [With the 'head' were] the needs for everything created, and afterward Elohim. And what is written after it? 'The Heavens and the Earth.' (Genesis 1:1)."
text.10_Siman: [Rabbi Bun continued,] And what is ['Elohim also created one opposite the other' (Ecclesiastes 7:14)? [God] created bohu and put its place in peace and created tohu and put its place in evil. Bohu is in peace as it is said 'The One Who creates peace in His heights' (Job 25:2). This teaches that Michael, the right-hand prince of the Blessed Holy One, is water and hail, and Gavriel, the left-hand prince of the Blessed Holy One, is fire. And the Prince of Peace decides between them. Thus it was written, 'The One Who creates peace in His heights.'"
text.11_Siman: [Rabbi Bun continued,] "And from where do we learn that tohu is in evil? As it is written, 'The one makes peace and creates evil' (Isaiah 45:7). How is this? Evil is from tohu and peace is from bohu. [God] created tohu and put its place in evil, as it is said, 'The one who makes peace and creates evil.' [God] created bohu and placed it in peace, as it is said, The one who creates peace in His heights' (Job 25:2)."
text.12_Siman: And Rabbi Bun sat and expounded more, "Why is it written, '[God] forms light and creates darkness' (Isaiah 45:7)? [Since] there is substance in light, it is written, as ‘formation.’ [Since] there is not substance in darkness, it is written as ‘creation.’ As you say, '[God] forms mountains and creates wind' (Amos 4:13). And if you want, say, that light has existence in it, as it is written, 'And Elohim said, ‘Let there be light,’ and there is no existence except by making, [therefore] call it 'formation.' Darkness, since it does not involve making, only separation and setting aside, it is called ‘creation’ [בריאה], as it is said, 'So-and-so became healthy [הבריא].'"
text.13_Siman: [Rabbi Bun continued,] "Why is [the letter] Bet closed on all sides and open in the front? To teach you that it is the house [bayit] of the world and that the Blessed Holy One, is the place of the world yet the world is not His place. Don’t read 'Bet', rather 'bayit'. This what is written, 'With wisdom [בחכמה], a house is built, and with understanding [בתבונה], it is established' (Proverbs 24:3).”
text.14_Siman: [Rabbi Bun continued,] "And to what is [the letter] Bet similar? To a person that it is formed with wisdom: closed on all sides but open in its front. [But] the [letter] Aleph is open from its back. This is to say that the tail of the Bet is open from behind, and if it were not thus, humans would not be sustained. So too, if it were not for the Bet in the tail of the Aleph, the world would not be sustained."
text.15_Siman: Rabbi Rechumai said, "The light preceded the world since 'Cloud and fog surround Him' (Psalm 97:2), as it is said, 'And God said, ‘There will be light,’ and there was light' (Genesis 1:3). They said to Him, ‘Before the formation of Israel, your son, will You make him a crown?’ He responded ‘yes.’ To what parable is this comparable? To a king that yearned for a son and found a beautiful, richly-adorned, and exalted crown and rejoiced greatly. He said, 'This is for my son’s head, as it is beautiful for him!' They said to him, 'And you know that your son is worthy?' He replied 'Silence! Thusly, this arose in my mind, and it is known!' As it is said, 'And He thinks thoughts' (Samuel 2 14:14)."
text.16_Siman: Rabbi Amorai sat and expounded, “Why is [the letter] Aleph at the beginning [of the aleph-bet]? That she [the letter Aleph] was before everything, even the Torah."
text.17_Siman: [Rabbi Amorai continued,] “And why is [the letter] Bet close to her [the letter] Aleph]? Because she [Bet] was the beginning. And why does she have a tail? To show which place she was from. There are those that say from there the world is sustained."
text.18_Siman:
[Rabbi Amorai continued,] “And why is [the letter] Gimmel third? Because it has three parts, and to inform us that she bestows [גומלת] acts of lovingkindness."
[They asked him,] "And didn't Rabbi Akiva [already] say, ‘Why is Gimmel in three parts? Because she weans [גומלת], grows [מתגדלת], and sustains [מתקיימת],’ as it is said ‘And the boy grew up [ויגדל] and was weaned [ויגמל]' (Genesis 21:8)."
He said to them, "It is my words [that Rabbi Akiva said], for he grew up [גודל] and bestowed [גומל] lovingkindness to his neighbors, his people, and those who trusted him."
text.19_Siman:
[They asked,] “And why is there a tail at the bottom of Gimmel?"
[Rabbi Amorai] said, "The Gimmel has a head above and is similar to a pipe. What is a pipe? Something that draws [water] from above and empties below. So too, Gimmel draws by way of the head and empties by way of the tail. This is Gimmel.”
text.20_Siman:
[Note: there are different textual variations of this text. Here is the version on Sefaria.]
Rabbi Yochanon said, “On the second day, the angels were created, as it is written, 'He rafters the beams [of His upper chambers] in the waters' (Psalms 104:3), and it is written 'He makes the winds His messengers, fiery flames His servants' (Psalms 104:4)."
But Rabbi Levitas ben Tavros said, "Everyone, even Rabbi Yochanan, agrees that the water already existed. But it was on the second day that ''He rafters the beams [of His upper chambers] in the waters,' the one who 'makes the clouds his chariot,' and the one who 'walks on the wings of the wind.' But His messengers were not created until the fifth day."

[The Vilna Gaon's commentary suggests the following version.]
Rabbi Yochanan said, "The angels were created on the second day. It is therefore written, 'He rafters the beams [of His upper chambers] in the waters, making the clouds a chariot, moving on the wings of the wind" (Psalm 104:3). It is then written, 'He makes the wind His angels' (Psalms 104:4)."
Rabbi Chaninah said, "The creation of the angels was on the fifth day, as is said, 'And the birds that flew over the earth' (Genesis 1:20)."
Rabbi Lulyani ben Tavrai said, "All agree that they [the angels] were not created on day one."
text.21_Siman: [Rabbi Levitas ben Tavrus continued,] "And all agree that [the angels] were not created on the first day, lest people might say, 'Michael drew out the south of Heaven, Gabriel [drew out] the north, and the Blessed Holy One is the one who made order in the middle. Rather, I am YHVH, who makes everything, Who stretches out the heavens by myself, who spreads out the land, unaided [מאתי]' (Isaiah 44:24). It is written [as] ‘who is with me’ [מי אתי]. [To say,] 'I am He that planted this tree so that all of the world would delight in it. I laid everything in it, and I called its name 'all,' because everything depends upon it, everything comes out from it, everything needs it, to it everything looks, for it they wait, and, from there, souls fly in joy. I was by myself when I did this. An angel will not be aggrandized on it to say, 'I was before you,' because at the time that I laid out the earth, and planted and rooted this tree in her, I rejoiced together, and I rejoiced in them. Who was with Me [מי אתי] that I revealed to him my secret?'"
text.22_Siman:
Rabbi Rachumi said, “From your words, it could be learned that the Blessed Holy One created the needs of this world before the heavens.”
He [Rabbi Levitas ben Tavrus] replied, “Yes. ָA parable, to what it is similar: to a king who seeks to plant a tree in his garden. He searches throughout the whole garden to know if there is a spring of flowing water to place the tree upon, and he does not find one. He says, ‘I will dig for water, and I will bring forth a spring so that the tree can be sustained.’ He dug, and out came a spring flowing with living waters. Afterward, he planted the tree, and it stood and produced fruit. It was successful in its roots because it always drinks from the spring."
text.23_Siman:
Rabbi Yanai said, “The Earth was created before the Heavens, as it is said, ‘[In the day of YHVH God’s making of the] Earth and the Heavens' (Genesis 2:4).’”
They said to him, “Isn’t it written ‘[In the beginning, God created] the Heavens and the Earth’ (Genesis 1:1)?”
He said to them, "To what does this compare? To a king who acquires a beautiful object, but it was not complete, so he did not give it a name. He said, ‘I will complete it and prepare its pedestal and accessories, and then I will give it a name.’ Thus it is written, ‘From eternity You established the Earth’ (Psalms 102:6), and afterward ‘And Heaven is the work of Your hands’ (Psalms 102:26). And it says, ‘He covered Himself with a garment of light, spread out the Heavens like a curtain, and set the waters as the rafters of His chambers’ (Psalms 104:2-3). Futher, it says, ‘He makes the winds His messengers and fiery flames His servants’ (Psalms 104:4), and afterward ‘He established the Earth on its foundation so that it will never [עולם ועד] be moved’ (Psalms 104:5). When He completed the pedestal, [the Earth] was strengthened by it, as is said, 'It will never be moved.’ What is its name? ‘Va’ed' [ועד] and the pedestal is ‘Earth' [עולם], thus it is ‘Olam Va’ed' [עולם ועד].”
text.24_Siman: Rabbi Berachyah said, “Why is it written, ‘And Elohim said, ‘Let there be light,’ and there was [ויהי] light’ (Genesis 1:3), and not, ‘And there was [והיה] light’? A parable: a king that had a nice object and set it aside until he prepared for it a place and put it there. As it is written, 'Let there be light, and there was light' — that it already was [היה]."
text.25_Siman: Rabbi Amorai said, “Why is it written, ‘YHVH is a man of war’ (Exodus 15:3)?" Mar Rachumai said to him, "My teacher, you should not ask a simple word! Hear me, and I will advise you." He [Mar Rachumai] said to him, "To what may this be compared? To a king who had beautiful dwellings, who gave a name to every single one of them, and each one of them was better than the last. He said, 'I will give this dwelling that is named Aleph to my son. But the one named Yud is also good, and the one named Shin is also good!' What did he do? He gathered together all three, made one name from them, and made one house from them." He [Rabbi Amorai] said to him, "Until when will you conceal your words?!" He [Mar Rachumai] said to him, "My son, Aleph is first, Yud is second to her, Shin includes the whole world. Why does Shin include the whole world? Because teshuvah [repentance] is written with her."
text.26_Siman: His [Mar Rachumai's] students asked him, “What is Dalet?” He said to them, "To what can this be compared? To ten kings that were in the same place. Though all of them were rich, one of them was not as wealthy as the others. Even though he was very wealthy, he is called poor [dal] in relation to the wealthy ones.
text.27_Siman: They said to him [Mar Rachumai], "What is Hei? He was angry and said to them, "Did I not say to you not to ask me about a later thing and afterward about the previous?" They said to him, "But Hei is written after [Dalet]!" He said to them, "It is fitting for it to have been written, ' Gimmel Hei,' so why is it written, ' Gimmel Dalet'?" He said to them, "The Gimmel was switched in place of Dalet, in the head in the place of Hei. Dalet in the embellishment of the place of Hei."
text.28_Siman: [Mar Rachumai's students asked him,] "What is Hei?" He said, "Lower Hei and upper Hei."
text.29_Siman:
[Mar Rachumai's students] said to him, "What is Vav?"
He said to them, "With six borders, the world is sealed."
They said to him, "But isn't Vav one?"
He said to them, "Is it not written, 'He spreads light like a garment' (Psalms 104:2)?"
text.30_Siman: Rabbi Amorai said, "Where is the Garden of Eden?" He [Mar Rachumai] said to him, "On the Earth."
text.31_Siman: [Mar Rachumai continued, citing an earlier teaching.] "Rabbi Ishmael expounded to Rabbi Akiva, 'What is it written, '[Et] the heavens and [et] the earth' (Genesis 1:1)? If it did not say this, people would say that the heavens and earth were gods.' He [Akiva] said to him, 'By the service of the divine! You touched [the verse], but you did not ascertain — and yet you spoke! [The word] et [serves to] include the sun, moon, stars, and constellations; v'et includes trees, grasses, and the Garden of Eden."
text.32_Siman: They [Mar Rachumai's students] said to him [Mar Rachumai], "Isn't it written, 'He has cast down from the heavens [to the] land, the majesty [tiferet] of Israel' (Lamentations 2:1), and, afterward, they fell." He said to them, "If you read it, you did not repeat it, and if you repeated it, you did not do it a third time! A parable, to what may this be compared? To a king that had a beautiful crown on his head and a beautiful cloak on his shoulders. An evil tiding came to him, and he cast the crown from his head and the cloak [note a mistake in the Sefaria Hebrew] from before him.
text.33_Siman: They [Mar Rachumai's students] asked him, "Why is Chet formed openly and vowelized with a small patach?" He said to them, "Because all the directions [ruchot] are closed except for the north, which is open for good and evil." They said to him, "For good?!? But isn't it written, 'And behold a stormy wind [ruach] came from the north, a great cloud and flashing fire' (Ezekiel 1:4). And there is not fire except furious anger, as is written, And fire went out from before YHVH and consumed them, and they died' (Leviticus 10:2)." He said to them, "This is not difficult. Here it is at a time when Israel does the will of The Place, while there is at a time when Israel does not do His will. At the time that Israel does not do His will, fire comes close, and at the time that they do His will, the trait of compassion rolls and surrounds, as it is written, 'Lifting up iniquity and passing over transgression' (Micah 7:18)."
text.34_Siman: [Mar Rachumai continued,] "A parable, to what can this be compared? To a king who wants to punish his servants and whip them. A leader stands and asks why. He says, 'Because of this.' He [the leader] says, 'Your servants never did this thing. I will be their guarantor, and you will investigate them, whether this or that.' The king's anger subsided.
text.35_Siman: His [Mar Rachumai's] students asked and said, "Why is Dalet thick on the side?" He said to them, "Because the segol is in the small patach, as is said, 'Openings of the world' (Psalms 24:7). He placed there a patach above and a segol below, and it becomes thick."
text.36_Siman: [Mar Rachumai's students asked,] "What is patach?" [He said,] "An opening [petach]." [They asked,] "And what is an opening?" [He replied,] "It is a north wind, which opens to the whole world. From the gate through which the evil came out, the good comes out." [They asked,] "And what is 'good'?” He mocked them, "Didn't I say to you, 'a small patach'?" They said to him, "We forgot. Teach us." He repeated [the teachings from 34 and 36, above]. He said to them, "To what can this be compared? To a king who has a throne. Sometimes he takes it on his arm and sometimes on his head." They said to him, "Why?" [He replied,] "Because it is beautiful and [it would be] a pity to sit upon it." They said, "Where does he place it on his head?" He said to them, "In the open mem, as it is written, 'Truth sprouts from the land, and righteousness looks down from the heavens.' (Psalms 85:12)"
text.37_Siman: Rabbi Amorai sat and expounded, "Why is it written, 'YHVH loves the gates of Zion more than all the [other] dwellings of Jacob' (Psalms 87:2)? 'The gates of Zion' - these are the openings of the world. There is no gate that is not an opening, as we say, 'Open for us the gates of compassion' (High Holiday Prayers). Thus, the Blessed Holy One said, 'I love the gates of Zion, when they are open.' Why? Because they are from the side of evil. But when Israel are good before The Place and fitting to be opened to good, the Blessed Holy One loves them ' more than the dwellings of Jacob.' All of them are peace - as is written, 'And Jacob was a simple man, sitting in tents' (Genesis 25:27)."
text.38_Siman: [Rabbi Amorai continued,] "This is like two men: one is invited to do evil and did good, and one is invited to do good and did good. Who do they praise more? The one who is accustomed to do evil and did good; perhaps he will do it a second time, as is written, 'YHVH loves the gates of Zion more than the dwellings of Jacob' (Psalms 87:2), all of which are peace, as is written, 'And Jacob was a simple man, sitting in tents' (Genesis 25:27)."
text.39_Siman: His students asked him, “What is cholem?” He [Rabbi Amorai] said to them, “A soul [neshamah]. Its name is cholem because if you listen, your body will recover for the future of its builders, but if you rebel against it, your illnesses will return upon your head — so cholim are on her head."
text.40_Siman: And further, they said, "Every dream is in a cholem, and every white pearl is in a cholem, as is written, 'achlamah [ed. - one of the stones on the choshen, usually translated as chrystal or amethyst]' (Exodus 28:19)."
text.41_Siman: He said to them, "Enter and hear the details of the vowel points of the Torah of Moses." He sat and expounded to them, "Chirik hates [son'e] the wicked and chastises them, and on its side are jealousy, hatred, and contention. As it is written, "And gnash [chorek] their teeth [shinav] at them" (Psalms 37:12). Don't read chorek, rather rochek [distance]. Distance these traits from yourself and distance the evil from yourself. All the more so, goodness will cleave to you."
text.42_Siman: [He continued,] "Chirik — do not say chirik, rather 'kerach [bald or ice],' since every place where a chirik is attached remains bald [or ice], as is written, 'And cleared'(Exodus 34:7)."
text.43_Siman: [The students asked,] "And why is it that chirik is of the language of burning?" [He responded,] "Because it is a fire that burns all fires, as is written, 'And the fire of YHVH descended and consumed the offering, the wood, the stone, and the dust, and it licked up the water that was in the trench.' (1 Kings 18:38)."
text.44_Siman:
Mar [Rachumai] said, "As it is written, 'And all the nation saw the voices [hakolot — often translated as 'thunder'] and the lightning' (Exodus 20:15). Can voices be seen?!? Rather, all the nation saw the voices — those [seven] voices about which David spoke.
[1] 'A voice [kol] of YHVH is upon the waters; the God of Glory thunders, etc.' (Psalms 29:3).
[2] 'A voice of YHVH in strength' (Psalms 29:4), and it says, With the strength of My hand, I have done [it]' (Isaiah 10:13), and it says, 'My own hand founded the earth' (Isaiah 48:13).
[3] 'A voice of YHVH in majesty [hadar] ' (Psalms 29:4), and the text said, 'Glorious [hod] and majestic [hadar] are His deeds, and His righteousness [tzedek] stands forever.' (Psalms 101:3).
[4] 'A voice of YHVH shatters cedars' (Psalms 29:5). This is the bow that shatters cypress trees and cedar trees.
[5] 'A voice of YHVH kindles flames of fire'(Psalms 29: 7). This is the one who makes peace between water and fire, that cuts the strength of the fire and prevents it from licking up the water and prevents them from evaporating it.
[6] 'A voice of YHVH convulses the desert' (Psalms 29:8), as is said, 'And He does kindness [chesed] to His annointed, to David, and to his descendents forever [may be reading hyperliterally: and to seed him, to the world]' (Psalms 18:51), —moreso than the desert.
[7] 'A voice of YHVH causes hinds to calve, and strips forests bare; while in the divine temple all say 'Glory!'' (Psalms 29:9). It is written, 'I adjure you, O maidens of Jerusalem, by gazelles or by hinds of the field' (Song of Songs 2:7).
Thus you have learned that with seven voices the Torah was given. With all of them, the Lord of the World was revealed to them, and they saw Him. As it is written, 'And all the nation saw the voices' (Exodus 20:15)."
text.45_Siman: [Mar Rachumai continued,] "One text says, 'He bent the heavens and descended, a thick cloud below His feet' (2 Samuel 22:10), another text says, 'He came down upon Mount Sinai to the top of the mountain' (Exodus 19:20), and another text says, 'For from the heavens I spoke with you' (Exodus 20:19). How is this to be understood? A great fire was on the land, which was one voice, and the remainder of the voices were in the heavens, as is written 'From the heavens, you could hear His voice to instruct you; on the earth, you could see the great fire, and you heard His words from within the fire' (Deuteronomy 4:36). What is this great [fire]? And from where was the speech coming out? From within the fire, as it is said 'and you heard His words from within the fire' ?"
text.46_Siman: [Mar Rachumai continued,] "And what is, 'And an image you did not see, only a voice' (Deuteronomy 4:12)? This is as Moses said to Israel, 'For you did not see all the image' (Deuteronomy 4:15) — [you saw] an image but not the whole image. A parable, to what it is may be compared: To a king that stands above his servants, draped in a white robe. It's not enough for the awe of the kingdom that they look at his garments. Further, the king was too far away, but they heard his voice. Can they see his throat? You would say, 'No.' Thus, you learned that they saw an image but not the whole image. Thus, it is written, 'And an image you did not see, only a voice' and it is written, 'The voice [sound] of words you heard' (Deuteronomy 4:12)."
text.47_Siman: [Mar Rachumai continued,] "One text says, 'And all the people saw the voices' (Exodus 20:15), and another text says, 'You heard the voice of words' (Deuteronomy 4:12). How can this be? At first, 'they saw the voices.' What did they see? Seven voices about which David spoke. And at the end, they heard the speech that comes out from between them all. But have we not learned that [that they are] ten? The rabbis said that all of them [the commandments] were spoken in one utterance (BT Shevuot 20b). So too, all of them were spoken in one utterance. But there were seven utterances! There were seven voices, and regarding three of them, it is said, 'You heard the voice of words, but you did not see an image — only a voice' (Deuteronomy 4:12). Thus, you learned that all of them were spoken as one utterance, so that Israel would not err by saying that another had helped him or the angels [helped] as His voice alone could not be this strong. Because of this, he returned and included all of them."
text.48_Siman: [Mar Rachumai continued,] "Another interpretation: So that the world would not say, 'Since there are ten utterances [ma'amarot], corresponding to ten kings, perhaps they cannot speak with one mouth,' it is written "I am" (Exodus 20:2), and all ten are included in it. What are ten kings? Seven voices and three sayings [amarim]. And what are 'sayings'? 'And YHVH affirmed you [he'emir'cha] today' (Deuteronomy 26:18). And what are these three? As is written, 'The beginning of wisdom [chochmah] is — acquire wisdom; with all your acquisitions, acquire understanding [binah]' (Proverbs 4:7); as it is said, 'The soul of Shaddai gives them understanding' (Job 32:8) — the soul of Shaddai, She gives them understanding. What is the third? As the old man says to the child, 'Seek not things concealed from you, nor search those hidden from you. Reflect on that which is permitted to you; you have no business with secret matters' (BT Chagigah 13a)."
text.49_Siman: [Mar Rachumai continued,] it was taught, ' It is the glory of Elohim to conceal a word' (Proverbs 25:2). What is 'a word'? As it is said, 'Truth is the essence of Your word' (Psalms 119:160) [and] 'The glory of kings is to examine a word' (Proverbs 25:2). What is 'a word'? As is written, 'A word spoken in its proper form [אופניו]' (Proverbs 25:11). Do not read 'proper form' [אופניו], rather, 'His faces' [אפניו]."
text.50_Siman:
His students asked Rabbi Berachiah, "Accept our words before you!" He did not give them permission. One time, he did give them permission, but he* did this to check whether now they could direct their souls. "The first day," he examined them and said, "Let me hear your wisdom."
They opened and said, "'In the beginning' (Genesis 1:1) is one. [Two is:] 'Spirit that will wrap itself is from before me; souls I made' (Isaiah 57:16). [Three is:] 'The division [פלג] of Elohim is filled with water' (Psalms 65:10)."
[Rabbi Berachiah asked them,] "What is 'division'?"
[They answered,] "Thus you taught us, our rabbi,** that [God] took waters of creation and divided them, gave half in the heavens and half in the ocean sea, as is written, 'The division of Elohim is filled with water' — and through it, a person learns Torah. As rabbi Chama said, 'Through the merit of gemilut chasadim a person learns Torah. Similarly, it is written, All who are thirsty, go to water, and if he has no money [כסף], obtain food and eat' (Isaiah 55:1) — go to him and he will bestow kindness to you: obtain [or, 'understand'] and eat!'"
*[Ed. - Sefaria text reads "she," but other versions say, "he."]
**[Ed. - Sefaria text reads "we saw"; other versions of the text say "our rabbi."]
text.51_Siman:
[Rabbi Berachiah responded,] “Another interpretation: ’And if he has no silver [כסף], go to him’ (Isaiah 55:1) — [go to Him,] because He has silver! As is written, ’To me is the silver and to me is the gold’ (Chaggai 2:8). What is ’Mine is the silver and Mine is the gold’? A parable, to which this is similar: to a king who has two treasure houses, one of silver and one of gold. The name of the silver was in his right and that of gold was in his left. He said, ‘This [the silver] will be available and easy to bring out.’ He makes his words gentle, and cleaves to the poor, and directs them with calm, as is written, ’Your right hand, YHVH, glorious in strength’ (Exodus 15:6). And if one is happy with his portion — good — but if not, ’Your right hand, YHVH shatters the enemy’ (Exodus 15:6)."
[The students asked,] "What is ’Your right hand, YHVH shatters the enemy’?”
He said to them, “This is the gold, as is written, ’Mine is the silver and Mine is the gold.’”
text.52_Siman:
[Rabbi Berachiah continued,] "And why is it called gold [זהב]? Since three traits are included in it:
1) male, which is zayin;
2) the soul [נשמה], which is the heh and [includes] the five [ה] names of the soul, ruach [רוח], chayah [חיה], yechidah [יחידה], nefesh [נפש], and neshama [נשמה] — why was she [the soul] made in five? To be a throne to the zayin, as is written, 'For a higher one is protected by a higher one' (Ecclesiastes 5:7) — and,
3) the bet establishes them, as is said, In [ב] the beginning, created' (Genesis 1:1)."
text.53_Siman: [Rabbi Berachiah continued,] "And why was she created thusly? A parable, to which this is similar: to a king who had a beautiful and nice daughter, pleasant and complete, and he married her to the son of a king. He dressed, crowned, and adorned her, and gave her to him with a great dowry. Is it possible for the king to dwell outside his house [i.e., with her in her new house]? You would say, 'No.' Is it possible for him to sit all the day with her always? You would say, 'No.' How is [he to deal with] this? He placed a window between him and her, and every time that the daughter needed her father or the father needed his daughter, they would meet together by the window. As is written, 'All the glory of the daughter or a king is inside her, her dress is embroidered with gold' (Psalms 45:14)."
text.54_Siman:
[Rabbi Berachiah continued,] "And what is Bet? As is written at the end, 'With wisdom, a house is built [יבנה]' (Provers 24:3) — 'was built' [נבנה] is not said, rather, 'he will build' [יבנה]. In the future, the Blessed Holy One will build her and adorn her, beyond what she was, two–thousandfold, as we have said, 'What was it, that the Torah begins with a Bet?' As is written, 'I was with Him as an artisan, and I was a source of delight every day [יום יום]' (Proverbs 8:30) — two thousand years, that she was first [ראשית]."
[They asked him,] "Two? But doesn't the text say seven?"
[He replied,] "As is written, 'The light of the moon will be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun will be sevenfold' (Isaiah 30:26).* As we say, 'Just as the sun is to seven, so to, the moon is to seven.' Rather**, they said two thousand."
*[Ed. - some manuscripts include: 'Like the light of the seven days' of creation [בראשית]]
**[Ed. - some manuscripts show "rather" ’[אלא] as a possibility instead of "I" [אנא]. While this alternative is not universal, it makes more sense.]
text.55_Siman:
They said to him, "Until here, five. From here and onwards, what?"
He said to them, "I will explain gold first. Why gold? It teaches that judgment comes out from it. And if you incline your words the right or the left, you will be admonished by it."
text.56_Siman:
[Rabbi Berachiah continued,] "Why is it written, 'The light of the moon will be like the light of the sun, and the light of the sun will be sevenfold, like the light of the seven days [שבעת הימים]' (Isaiah 30:26). 'The days [הימים]'? It should have said 'days [ימים]'! But these are the days about whom it is written, 'Because six days YHVH made' (Exodus 31:17)."
His friend said to him, "This, I have received from what is written, 'Because six days YHVH made', like that which you said, 'The Blessed Holy One made six beautiful vessels.' What are they?"
[He continued,] 'The Heavens and the Earth' (Genesis 1:1)."
[His friend objected,] "But they are seven!"
[He continued,] "And therefore, it is written, 'On the seventh day, [God] stopped and rested [וינפש]' (Exodus 31:17). What is 'rested [וינפש]'? It teaches that the day of Shabbat establishes all souls [הנפשות], as is said, 'and [He] souled [וינפש].'"
text.57_Siman: [Rabbi Berachiah continued,] "Another interpretation: It teaches that souls fly out from there, as it is said, 'and [He] souled [וינפש]' (Exodus 31:17) until the thousandth generation, as is said, 'A word commanded to the thousandth generation' (Psalms 105:8). And next to it, 'That was cut with Abraham' (Psalms 105:9). What is 'that was cut'? [God] cut him a covenant between the ten fingers of his hand and then toes of his foot. Abraham was shamed. The Blessed Holy One said to him, 'Here, I have covenanted with you' (Genesis 17:4) and with it, you will be 'The father of a great nation' (Genesis 17:4)"
